SMTO-GIT-0002 — Your Git project changed while SMTO was reading it

GUID: 5184dd24-b801-46cd-b6f0-49a2899b0463
Slug: git-discovery-changed
Domain: GIT · Subsystem: git

What happened

  • SMTO was reading your Git project's settings, such as where it sends and gets changes, and they changed while it was reading. SMTO set that reading aside instead of using details that might be wrong. Your project wasn't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for any other Git activity on that project to finish, such as a pull, push or fetch, or an editor saving Git settings. Those programs rewrite the files SMTO was reading at that moment.
  2. If another Task in SMTO is working in the same project, let it finish first. Two Tasks using the same project can change its settings while the other is reading them.
  3. Then ask SMTO again for what you needed. With nothing changing the project, SMTO can read its settings in one consistent pass.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the project's details without this message.

If it still fails

  • If it happens every time, something keeps changing the project's settings; select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't reuse older project details SMTO gave you before the change; ask for fresh ones.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway Git discovery rejected an observation because a metadata or configuration file's descriptor revision (device, inode, size, mtime, ctime) changed while it was read, or a configuration file's revision differed before and after remote parsing.

What this means

  • A bounded metadata read changes revision/size during observation, or a configuration file's before/after revision differs. These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.

Why this can happen

  • A bounded metadata read changes revision/size during observation, or a configuration file's before/after revision differs.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the changing metadata/configuration file and concurrent writer before refreshing observation.

How to fix it

  • Identify concurrent writers to .git/config, config.worktree, gitfiles or the global/system gitconfig on the Gateway host (git fetch/pull, IDE integrations, sync tools) and let them settle, then rerun so discovery records matching before/after revisions. Persistent failures mean a tool is continually rewriting those files.
  • Wait for concurrent Git/configuration writers to finish and refresh discovery from the current stable repository.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A stable observation returns matching before/after revisions.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
